topic.title: Bayesian Graph Structure and Hierarchical Models
topic.area: Graphical Models, Clustering, and Network Structure
topic.overview: Bayesian structure learning infers relationships among variables while retaining uncertainty about the graph itself. These papers study bounded-treewidth networks, low-rank conditional models, incomplete temporal data, and differentiable graph distributions. Related hierarchical and tree-based models exploit structure to make posterior computation and interpretation manageable.
topic.whyItMatters: Selecting one graph can conceal multiple explanations compatible with limited observations. Posterior structure matters for interventions and subsequent inference, while computational constraints determine which dependencies can realistically be represented.
topic.evolution: Early representatives connect Bayesian model comparison and neural representations. Later work scales network learning through treewidth constraints and compact conditional tables. Recent methods place differentiable latent distributions over graphs and develop probabilistic routing on constrained domains, combining flexible structure with sparse computations and explicit uncertainty.
openQuestions: How can graph-posterior approximations preserve competing causal explanations?
When does enforcing tractable structure introduce more error than the resulting computational savings justify?
